deep.reconstruction:
NOTATION. p, p', p'', p''' are complex positions of the points (0),(1),(2),(3). A pair symbol such as 01 has two meanings. As a length or factor it is |p-p'|. Inside sin(...) it is the direction (argument) of the segment 01.

A. The 'Ptolemy triangle'. Gauss takes the triangle with vertices
(4) P4 = pp' + p''p''',
(5) P5 = pp'' + p'''p',
(6) P6 = pp''' + p'p''.
Its side vectors are (my verification):
- P5 - P6 = (p-p')(p''-p''')
- P6 - P4 = (p-p'')(p'''-p')
- P4 - P5 = (p-p''')(p'-p'')
The three products listed on the page therefore sum to zero. This is Euler's four-point identity.

The marginal labels '65, 46, 54' name these sides as vertex pairs. For example, side 65 has length 01·23 and direction (01)+(23), because arguments add under multiplication. Likewise side 46 is 02·31 with direction (02)+(31), and side 54 is 03·12 with direction (03)+(12).

The angle of this triangle opposite side 65 is the difference of the directions of the other two sides: (02+31)-(03+12). The law of sines (in the form sin A / a = const) then gives
sin(02+31-03-12)/(01·23) = sin(03+12-01-23)/(02·31) = sin(01+23-02-31)/(03·12) = Ω.
Here Ω = 1/(2R'), with R' the circumradius of the Ptolemy triangle. Equivalently Ω = 2·Area'/(01·23·02·31·03·12), with a sign fixed by orientation. The triangle inequality for this triangle is Ptolemy's inequality. Ω = 0 (degenerate triangle) is exactly Ptolemy's equality, i.e. the four points are concyclic.

B. Expanding one of the expressions (Gauss refers to p. 284 for this), Gauss states
Ω = [01·sin(03-02) + 02·sin(01-03) + 03·sin(02-01)] / (12·13·23).
Check (mine): put the origin at point 0 and let a, b, c be the positions of 1, 2, 3. Then 2·Area' = Im(conj(-c(a-b))·(-a(b-c))). This equals, up to sign,
|a|^2 Im(conj(b)c) + |b|^2 Im(conj(c)a) + |c|^2 Im(conj(a)b) = |a||b||c|·[|a| sin(γ-β) + |b| sin(α-γ) + |c| sin(β-α)].
Dividing by the six lengths gives Gauss's formula up to orientation sign. The numerator D = det[[r^2, x, y]] over the rows 1, 2, 3 (origin at 0) vanishes iff 0 lies on the circle through 1, 2, 3.

C. Write Ω^{0123} for this quantity.

Setting (my interpretation). Points (1)-(4) are fixed. Point (0) is movable, and the orientation is also variable. So 01, 02, 03, 04 in the differentials are the directions observed at 0 toward the four fixed points. This is the resection (Snellius-Pothenot) problem with one surplus direction: there are four observations and three unknowns (x, y, orientation).

Derivation (mine). Let θ_k = arg(p_k - z) - ω. Then dθ_k = -Im(dz/(p_k - z)) - dω. A linear relation Σ c_k dθ_k = 0 holds identically iff Σ c_k = 0 and Σ c_k/(p_k - z) = 0 (complex). These are three real conditions, so c is unique up to scale. With origin at z, 1/a_k = conj(a_k)/r_k^2. Hence c_k is proportional to the alternating cofactors of the rows (1, x_k/r_k^2, y_k/r_k^2), i.e. c_k ∝ (-1)^{k+1} r_k^2 D_{jlm}.

Gauss's coefficients reduce to the same thing. For example c_1 = 01·23·24·34·Ω^{0234} = 01·N_{234} = r_1^2 D_{234}/(r_1 r_2 r_3 r_4). So the condition equation
01·23·24·34·Ω^{0234} d01 - 02·13·14·34·Ω^{0134} d02 + 03·12·14·24·Ω^{0124} d03 - 04·12·13·23·Ω^{0123} d04 = 0
is correct. A coefficient vanishes when 0 is concyclic with the other three points, which is the 'danger circle' of resection.

D. Footnote (partly struck, replaced by 'Besser wie bemerkt'). Let g + g' + g'' = 0 be the side vectors of a triangle and h, h', h'' their 'Adjuncten' (complex conjugates). Then the imaginary parts of gh', g'h'', g''h are equal, and each is 2i times the triangle's area (up to sign). Proof given: gh' - g'h'' = gh' + hg' + g'h', which is real. It is real because g'h = conj(gh') and g'h' = |g'|^2. All correct.

This is the lemma that underlies step A.
errors: No substantive errors. All identities hold up to the orientation sign convention for angles, which Gauss leaves implicit.

Sign of Ω: with a fixed counterclockwise convention, the 'Ptolemy triangle' expression and the expanded formula in B differ by an overall sign unless the orientation of the triangle 456 is chosen appropriately. This is a convention issue, not an error.

'Orientirung auch als veränderlich' combined with differentials d01...d04 only makes sense if these denote direction differentials (as in resection), not distance differentials. Gauss does not state this explicitly.

results.what: (p-p')(p''-p''') + (p-p'')(p'''-p') + (p-p''')(p'-p'') = 0, realized as the side vectors of the triangle with vertices pp'+p''p''' etc.
results.modern_name: Euler's four-point identity; complex-number proof of Ptolemy's inequality (Ptolemy triangle)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (identity); the complex-number treatment of Ptolemy's inequality is 19th-century folklore (e.g. Möbius-era/Cauchy-era geometry)

results.what: Law of sines for the Ptolemy triangle: sin(02+31-03-12)/(01·23) = ... = Ω, vanishing iff the four points are concyclic
results.modern_name: Ptolemy's theorem/inequality via the triangle with sides ac, bd, ef; relation to Euler's pedal-triangle area theorem

results.what: Ω = [01 sin(03-02) + 02 sin(01-03) + 03 sin(02-01)]/(12·13·23), i.e. the concyclicity determinant det[r^2, x, y] normalized
results.modern_name: Concyclicity (circle) determinant / power of point 0 w.r.t. circle 123

results.what: Condition equation among the direction differentials d01..d04 at a station 0 observing four fixed points with unknown orientation, with coefficients ±(lengths)·Ω^{0jkl}
results.modern_name: Condition equation for over-determined resection (four-point Pothenot/Snellius problem); coefficients vanish on the 'danger circle'
results.usually_credited_to: Geodetic adjustment literature (Gauss, Gerling, later Helmert/Jordan); danger-circle discussion usually attributed to 19th-century geodesy

results.what: For a triangle with side vectors g+g'+g''=0 and conjugates h, the imaginary parts of gh', g'h'', g''h are equal (= 2i·area)
results.modern_name: Signed area via Im(z1·conj(z2)); cross-product invariance

deep.surprise_reason: The complex-number treatment of the quadrilateral (Euler identity, Ptolemy triangle, concyclicity determinant) is routine. Gauss's use of complex positions for plane geometry is well known. The elegant closed-form condition equation for four-point resection, with coefficients expressed through the Ω's (vanishing on the danger circle), is a notable unpublished geodetic detail. It is consistent with Gauss's known resection work, so it is mildly rather than strongly surprising.

checkable.asserts: Euler four-point identity: the three products are side vectors of a closed triangle
Vertex (5) minus vertex (6) equals (p-p')(p''-p''') (side 65 has size 01·23)
Twice the Ptolemy-triangle area equals (minus) the expanded numerator; this gives Gauss's formula for Ω up to orientation sign
Footnote lemma: Im(g h') = Im(g' h'') when g+g'+g''=0 and h = conj(g)

checkable.sympy: D=lambda A,B,C: abs(A)**2*im(conjugate(B)*C)+abs(B)**2*im(conjugate(C)*A)+abs(C)**2*im(conjugate(A)*B); c1=abs(a1)**2*D(a2,a3,a4); c2=-abs(a2)**2*D(a1,a3,a4); c3=abs(a3)**2*D(a1,a2,a4); c4=-abs(a4)**2*D(a1,a2,a3); simplify(c1+c2+c3+c4)==0 and simplify(c1/a1+c2/a2+c3/a3+c4/a4)==0
checkable.asserts: Gauss's coefficients (reduced to r_k^2 D) satisfy Σc_k=0 and Σc_k/(p_k-z)=0 (origin at z), so Σ c_k dθ_k = 0 for arbitrary dz and dω
Numerator of Ω^{0123} (origin-free form) is this determinant; it is zero iff the points 0,1,2,3 are concyclic (Ptolemy equality)

transcription_corrections: The marginal '65, 46, 54' are vertex pairs of the triangle (sides 6-5, 4-6, 5-4), not numerical values.
The minus signs before the 2nd and 4th lines of the differential equation are blotted in the image but are real; the signs alternate +,-,+,-.
In the footnote, 'Adjuncten jener Grössen, so sind die imaginären Theile von gh', g'h'', g''h gleich' reads naturally ('Adjuncten' = complex conjugates). 'und nemlich' is probably 'indem nemlich'.
Footnote equation: gh' - g'h'' = gh' + hg' + g'h', which is real. This is consistent with g+g'+g''=0 and h+h'+h''=0.
'(wie?)' is a faint pencil annotation near a small sketch, not part of the formulas.
In the first fraction of the sine-law equation, '02+31' is written over a correction.
